bound_context.question: What does the 136-byte leaf routine at 0x630b9c0 do to a deflate_state, what does it leave in rax, and what does it assume about its caller?
bound_context.version_note: node115 embeds ZLIB_VERSION "1.3.1"; these bodies are identical in the zlib 1.3.2 bundled by libz-sys 1.1.31, so the zlib release is not pinned by these windows.

consumer_table.meaning: rax is clobbered by an unrelated value at every site before it could be read

caller_census.contract: void-style: the routine's effect is entirely through its first argument, and whatever it leaves in rax is a leftover (bi_valid, the old pending count, or 0 depending on the path) - every one of the 26 call sites overwrites rax before reading it
caller_census.method: every call target matching the window start is decoded with Capstone and attributed to the enclosing .eh_frame FDE; the instruction after the call is classified by how rax is first used

claim_anchors: semantics.tsv (20 anchors: claim -> target instruction address, bytes and decoded instruction)
environment_limits: the packet is static: the artifact is never executed and no source build is claimed
the emulator implements only the instructions this routine uses and raises on any other
the modelled deflate_state is a synthetic struct at a fixed address; real callers reach the same fields at different addresses

layouts.name: deflate_state (fields touched by this window)

fields.+0x10: pending_out, pointer to the output buffer
fields.+0x28: pending, u64 count of bytes written
fields.+0x1734: bi_valid, u32 count of valid bits

layouts.note: +0x20 (pending_buf_size) is NOT touched: no store is bounds checked

ledger: cases.tsv (300 reviewable cases, 60 per family: 0..7, 8..15, 17..0x7fffffff, 0x80000000..0xffffffff and exactly 16) recording bi_valid, bi_buf, pending, the emitted bytes, the new field values and the rax leftover; the boundary rows are kept verbatim and the full 2,400-case sweep is re-derived in memory by the tests

observations.text: the window 0x630b9c0..0x630ba48 is one .eh_frame FDE, 136 bytes, 32 instructions, a leaf with no calls and no relocations
the dispatch is three-way: bi_valid == 16 emits two bytes, bi_valid <= 7 emits nothing, and every other value emits exactly one byte
the <= 7 test is a SIGNED jle on the 32-bit field, so every value with bit 31 set emits nothing even though the field is an unsigned count
out-of-range but positive values behave as the one-byte path: 17 -> 9, 18 -> 10, 23 -> 15, 24 -> 16, 100 -> 92
the pending counter is written with pending+1 BEFORE the byte store, and the store uses the pre-increment index, so the byte lands at pending_out[old pending]
the two-byte emit is little-endian: pending_out[p] gets bi_buf & 0xff and pending_out[p+1] gets bi_buf >> 8, in ascending address order
the 8..15 path shifts bi_buf down by 8 as a 2-byte read-modify-write and subtracts 8 from bi_valid as a 4-byte one
the 16 path zeroes bi_buf with a 2-byte store and bi_valid with a 4-byte store; it does not mask or merge
rax is left holding bi_valid on the nothing-to-do path, the old pending count on the one-byte path, and 0 on the two-byte path: three different leftovers, so it is not a status
all 26 direct call sites overwrite rax before reading it, which is consistent with the leftovers carrying no information
no store is bounds checked: pending_buf_size (+0x20) is never read and no pointer is compared with a limit
the argument is deflate_state* (a struct whose touched fields are at +0x10, +0x28, +0x1730 and +0x1734) and the routine is zlib's bit-flush step, read off the struct usage rather than a symbol
the caller is responsible for having space for two more bytes in the pending buffer, since the body cannot check it
in normal zlib use bi_valid never exceeds 16, so the one-byte path is reached only for 8..15; the behaviour outside that invariant is documented here but is not reachable from a conforming caller

unknowns: the real callers' invariants (buffer space, bi_valid <= 16) are inferred from zlib's contract and the absence of checks, not verified against any caller
the zlib release is not pinned by this window (the census records that these bodies are identical in the zlib 1.3.2 bundled by libz-sys 1.1.31)
the body is byte-identical in 3 identical source objects; only 0x630b9c0 is bound
whether pending_out can be null in some caller state is not characterized here
which of the 26 call sites are reachable for a given compression is not characterized
